page.layout: One printed page, single column of running text; a small margin note "Cap. 10." at the left beside the heading line "De Cineribus"; page number and running head at the top.

main_text.l: III. Vt mentes & corda nostra, inuisibili igne & splendore sancti Spiritus illustrentur, omniumque peccatorum & vitiorum cæcitate careant, vt cernere possimus quæ Deo sunt placita & vtilia saluti.
IIII. Vt ignis Charitatis cum lumine fidei in animis nostris accendatur, qui nos ad lumen indeficiens in vitam æternam deducat.
main_text.p: Cap. 10.De Cineribus similis est ratio. Petit, (inquis) multis orationibus in cinerum benedictione ecclesia, vt istos salutares effectus consequantur fideles, qui sunt his cineribus vsuri.
main_text.l: I. Vt iuuetur Homo ad internam humilitatem cordis.

II. Vt benedictio cælestis in aspersos descendat, qua serio compungantur & de peccatis doleant; considerantes per peccatum hominis & ipsam terram maledictam fuisse in opere nostro, & nos omnes in terram & cinerem reditur和s.
III. Vt hi cineres sint salubre remedium ad assequendam remissionem peccatorum & præmium vitæ æterna.
IIII. Vt detur corporis sanitas, ad pœnitentiam pro peccatis agendam.

page.notes: Line "II." reads "rediturōs" in print; the word "rediturōs" is printed as "rediturōs." The marginal "Cap. 10." is printed in bold beside the heading. The final line "v. Vt" is a catchword-like signature at the lower right, not a full line. Some letters of the scan are faint; the Latin is transcribed as read, with some doubtful words in the line II and the closing "v. Vt" uncertain.
